newsitem.title: NIGERIA: New bank shares lift Nigerian stock market.
newsitem.headline: New bank shares lift Nigerian stock market.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market closed higher on Friday on the back of a generous price rise and the good run of newly-listed Guaranty Trust Bank.

Many active sectors benefitted from the rise, which sent the all-share index soaring to 6,250.83, up by 28.65 points from Thursday. Shares of Guaranty Trust Bank were the toast of the market, appreciating by the maximum five percent allowed per day to 12.58 naira. It closed at 11.60 naira on Thursday.
Traders said public euphoria about the stock was responsible for the strong showing since its listing on Monday.
"Everybody is excited about the shares," Mike Itegboje, chief executive officer of TRW Stockbrokers, told Reuters. "There is euphoria right now."
The shares were listed on Monday at 10.00 naira per share, giving its owners a 21.8 percent rise in five days.
Oil shares also ended well up. Unipetrol added 45 kobo to 35.60 naira, while Total rose by 40 kobo to 44.00 naira.
West African Portland Cement advanced by 40 kobo to 29.50 naira and construction firm G. Cappa finished strongly at 6.02 naira, a 22 kobo rise.

Cadbury and Flour Mills added 20 kobo each, closing at 24 naira and 9.50 naira, respectively. PZ Industries led conglomerates with a 30 kobo rise to 33.90 naira, followed by Lever Brothers, which chalked 10 kobo to 24.85 naira.
Friday's big losers were Nigerian Breweries and Guinness. Both fell 20 kobo, respectively, to 13.10 naira and 9.30 naira due to the large volumes investors wanted to offload.
Lack of buyers also hit French trading firm CFAO, which slid by 10 kobo to 5.10 naira, as well as NAL Merchant Bank, down three kobo at 5.70 naira.
Traders said the excitement that greeted the listing of Guaranty Trust Bank would sustain interest in its shares and propel it to rise further next week.
"Many people are still clamouring for it because it represents to them a stock with good prospects," said Bayo Adeniji of securities research firm Hamilton Hammer.
Traders said brewing and packaging firms looked set to continue their slide in the near future.
